old: This leaves the lead in milligrams while the water is in grams. Use the same unit for both masses.
new: 0.025 is the lead concentration in milligrams per liter, which is ppm, not ppb. Multiply by 1000 to convert ppm to ppb.
why: 0.050 mg / 2.00 L = 0.025 mg/L = 0.025 ppm; leaving Pb in mg over water in g would give 2.5×10⁴, not 0.025

old: Removing H+ from HCO3− leaves CO32−: the same C and three O atoms, no H, and a 2− charge (two O atoms carry −1). H2CO3 is the conjugate acid, CO2 has lost an O and an OH, and formate (HCO2−) has lost an O atom rather than an H+.
new: Removing H+ from HCO3− leaves CO32−: the same C and three O atoms, no H, and a 2− charge (two O atoms carry −1). H2CO3 is the conjugate acid, CO2 has lost a whole OH− (an O as well as the H), and formate (HCO2−) has lost an O atom rather than an H+.
why: HCO3- -> CO2 + OH- removes one O and one H, not 'an O and an OH'

old: Ag2CrO4 begins when [Ag+]2(0.010) = 1.1×10−12, so [Ag+] = 1.0×10−5 M. At that [Ag+], [Cl−] = 1.8×10−10 / 1.0×10−5 = 1.7×10−5 M, so over 99.8% of the chloride has already precipitated. 1.0×10−5 M is [Ag+], not [Cl−].
new: Ag2CrO4 begins when [Ag+]2(0.010) = 1.1×10−12, so [Ag+] = 1.05×10−5 M. At that [Ag+], [Cl−] = 1.8×10−10 / 1.05×10−5 = 1.7×10−5 M, so over 99.8% of the chloride has already precipitated. 1.0×10−5 M is [Ag+], not [Cl−].
